---
title: "Week 4 — Turning Data into New Information"
subtitle: "Operators, expressions, evaluation order, and computational transformation"
---

::: {.callout-tip}
## This week's central question

**How does a program transform existing values into new information?**
:::

## Learning goals

By the end of this week, you should be able to:

1. distinguish a **value**, an **operator**, and an **expression**;
2. use arithmetic operators to transform numeric data;
3. predict the result of expressions before running code;
4. explain how assignment stores the result of an expression;
5. use parentheses to make evaluation order explicit;
6. write readable expressions with standard spacing and descriptive result names;
7. identify and repair incorrect formulas.

## Connection

Week 3 gave values meaningful names and representations. Week 4 combines those values into new information.

A readable expression should make the domain relationship visible, not merely produce the right number.

::: {.callout-note}
## Make the relationship visible

Prefer:

```python
total_revenue = quantity_sold * unit_price
profit_margin = profit / revenue
```

over compressed forms such as:

```python
r=q*p
m=p/r
```

Python ignores most of the visual difference. Human readers do not.
:::
